paragraphs: A time-series generator can produce plausible sequences while failing to reproduce the range of behaviors present in its training data. This paper formalizes that failure, called mode collapse, and introduces DMD-GEN to measure it. The central idea is to compare the temporal dynamics of real and generated sequences, making diversity a question about how signals evolve.

DMD-GEN uses Dynamic Mode Decomposition to extract coherent temporal structures. It represents the subspaces formed by the resulting eigenvectors as points on a Grassmann manifold, a geometric space for comparing subspaces. Principal angles describe their geometric differences, while optimal transport and Wasserstein distances turn those comparisons into a measure of disagreement between real and generated dynamics.

The metric requires no additional model training, supports mini-batches, and can run in parallel. It also identifies dynamical modes that are missing or distorted, helping explain a poor score. Experiments with TimeGAN, TimeVAE, and DiffusionTS on synthetic and real data show agreement with existing metrics while adding a geometric interpretation of lost temporal diversity.
neurips-2025-a-geometry-aware-metric-for.tldr: DMD-GEN measures and interprets missing diversity in generated time series by comparing the geometry of their temporal dynamics.

paragraphs: Grokking describes a training pattern in which a model fits its training examples early but improves on test examples much later. This paper investigates whether optimization itself can explain that delay. It studies continuous-time gradient flow with small weight decay, which encourages parameters to have a smaller overall magnitude.

Under mild regularity assumptions and convergence of the unregularized gradient flow, the authors establish two phases as weight decay approaches zero. Initially, the parameters follow approximately the path they would take without weight decay, reaching a manifold of critical points of the training loss. On a timescale proportional to the inverse weight-decay strength, a slower motion then emerges.

That slow motion follows a Riemannian gradient flow that reduces parameter norm while respecting the geometry of the critical-point manifold. The authors argue that this delayed norm reduction can account for a later jump in generalization. Experiments on synthetic regression tasks support the proposed mechanism. The result offers an optimization-based explanation for grokking under the stated assumptions, rather than establishing that every observed grokking event has this cause.
neurips-2025-a-theoretical-framework-for.tldr: Under stated assumptions, small weight decay produces a slow norm-reduction phase that offers an explanation for delayed generalization.

paragraphs: Detecting unusual events from a drone requires handling changing viewpoints, varying object sizes, and complex scenes. A2Seek addresses this setting with a benchmark built from high-resolution aerial videos. Its annotations describe anomaly categories, when events happen, where they appear, and natural-language explanations intended to support reasoning about their causes.

The accompanying A2Seek-R1 framework combines several ways of developing that reasoning. Graph-of-thought guidance structures supervised fine-tuning, while Aerial Group Relative Policy Optimization supplies rule-based rewards tailored to aerial scenes. A separate seeking mechanism directs attention toward informative regions, taking inspiration from how a UAV moves to investigate a scene.

Together, the dataset and framework target both locating anomalies and explaining why they occur. The experiments report improvements of up to 22.04% in average precision for prediction and a 13.9% gain in mean intersection-over-union for localization. The authors also report strong generalization across complex environments and out-of-distribution scenarios. These findings support evaluating aerial anomaly systems on spatial understanding and reasoning alongside event prediction.
neurips-2025-a2seek-towards-reasoning-ce.tldr: A2Seek pairs annotated aerial videos with a reasoning framework that improves anomaly prediction, localization, and understanding in the reported experiments.

paragraphs: Reinforcement learning can strengthen language-model reasoning, but training often requires several generated responses per prompt and costly estimates of response quality. A-star-PO addresses this overhead by separating value estimation from subsequent policy updates. Its target is an approximation of the optimal advantage function, which guides how the model should improve its choices.

The first stage samples offline from a reference policy to estimate the optimal value function. The second stage updates the current model with a least-squares regression objective and only one generated response per prompt. This organization removes the need for expensive online value estimation during those updates and reduces the generation burden.

The authors establish performance guarantees and show that the KL-regularized reinforcement-learning objective can be optimized without complex exploration strategies. On mathematical reasoning benchmarks, the method achieves competitive performance while reporting up to a twofold reduction in training time and more than 30% lower peak memory usage compared with PPO, GRPO, and REBEL. The findings connect a different training target with practical savings in reasoning-model fine-tuning.
neurips-2025-accelerating-rl-for-llm-rea.tldr: A-star-PO separates offline value estimation from single-response policy updates to reduce the cost of training language models for reasoning.

paragraphs: Structured sparsity encourages whole groups of neural-network weights to disappear, producing more compact models. The penalties used to induce this behavior are often non-differentiable, complicating ordinary gradient-based training. D-Gating tackles that difficulty by representing each weight group through a primary vector and several scalar gates, yielding a fully differentiable objective.

The authors prove a specific connection to the original sparsity problem: every local minimum under D-Gating is also a local minimum for the corresponding non-smooth structured L2,2/D penalty. They additionally show that, in the gradient-flow limit, the D-Gating objective approaches the regularized loss at least exponentially fast. These results give the smooth formulation a formal relationship to structured penalization.

Despite that relationship, its training trajectory differs: optimization begins in a non-sparse regime and evolves toward sparse optimization. Experiments across vision, language, and tabular tasks report strong tradeoffs between predictive performance and sparsity, outperforming direct structured-penalty optimization and conventional pruning baselines. The contribution combines a differentiable training mechanism with guarantees about the sparsity objective it represents.
neurips-2025-differentiable-sparsity-via.tldr: D-Gating provides a differentiable route to structured sparsity with theoretical links to non-smooth penalties and strong empirical performance–sparsity tradeoffs.

paragraphs: This paper studies how to publish useful, differentially private answers when the underlying dataset keeps changing. The queries are linear, and the aim is to keep the error in their released answers small. Although this problem is well studied for a fixed dataset, the setting here requires answers at every time step.

The stream is fully dynamic: items can be added and removed. Consequently, the mechanism must support continuing releases while the data changes in both directions. This differs from answering queries once about a static collection. The paper focuses on transferring existing solutions for that static problem into this more demanding setting.

The main result is a set of efficient black-box constructions that turn static private mechanisms into dynamic ones. Black-box use means the static mechanism serves as a component of the construction. The resulting utility degrades by only a polylogarithmic factor. This establishes that supporting continual answers with insertions and deletions can be achieved with a controlled loss in answer quality, while reusing mechanisms developed for static data.
neurips-2025-differential-privacy-on-ful.tldr: The paper converts static differential-privacy mechanisms into efficient mechanisms for continual answers under insertions and deletions, with polylogarithmic utility degradation.

paragraphs: The paper introduces a neural framework for predicting travel-time fields governed by the Eikonal equation. A single shared neural field represents multiple solutions, with each solution specified by its own latent variables. Those variables take the form of point clouds in a Lie group, giving the representation an explicit connection to geometric transformations.

The key property is equivariance: transforming the latent point cloud produces a predictable geometric change in the output field. This makes solutions steerable and supports weight sharing across them. The framework combines these representations with physics-informed neural networks so that the predicted fields model Eikonal travel-time solutions.

The formulation extends to Riemannian manifolds with regular group actions, including Euclidean, position–orientation, spherical, and hyperbolic spaces. That geometric condition defines the stated scope of the generalization. Experiments on seismic travel-time benchmarks in two dimensions, three dimensions, and spherical settings report better performance, scalability, adaptability, and user control than existing neural-operator Eikonal solvers. The approach ties reusable representations and controllable outputs to the geometry of the solution space.
neurips-2025-equivariant-eikonal-neural-.tldr: Equivariant Neural Eikonal Solvers use shared, geometrically steerable representations to predict travel-time fields across supported curved and flat spaces.

paragraphs: BTimer reconstructs a dynamic scene at a chosen instant from a monocular video, meaning a video captured through one camera view at a time. The resulting bullet-time representation supports viewing that frozen moment from new viewpoints. This addresses a difficulty for feed-forward reconstruction systems developed around static scenes: moving content changes across the available frames.

The model aggregates information from all context frames to reconstruct the complete scene at the requested timestamp. It represents that scene using 3D Gaussian Splatting. By making a target moment the focus of reconstruction, the formulation can draw on both static and dynamic scene datasets, which the authors identify as a source of scalability and generalization.

The reported system reconstructs a bullet-time scene from a casual monocular dynamic video within 150 milliseconds. It also achieves state-of-the-art performance on the evaluated static and dynamic datasets, including comparisons with optimization-based methods. The findings show that the reported fast reconstruction approach can handle scene motion while producing competitive novel views, connecting dynamic reconstruction quality with real-time operation.
neurips-2025-feed-forward-bullet-time-re.tldr: BTimer reconstructs a dynamic scene at a chosen moment from monocular video in 150 milliseconds, enabling high-quality novel views.

paragraphs: This paper asks how many samples are needed to evaluate a policy in a robust average-reward Markov decision process. Earlier results established eventual convergence, but did not quantify the data required to reach a given accuracy. The contribution is a finite-sample analysis covering both robust policy evaluation and robust average-reward estimation.

The analysis first shows that the robust Bellman operator contracts under a carefully chosen semi-norm, providing a way to control estimation errors. The authors then develop a stochastic-approximation framework that allows controlled bias. Multi-Level Monte Carlo supplies efficient estimates of the operator, but the standard approach considered here has infinite expected sample cost.

A truncation mechanism based on a geometric distribution resolves that cost problem. It makes expected sampling finite while introducing a small bias that decreases exponentially with the truncation level. Combining these ingredients yields order-optimal sample complexity proportional to the inverse square of the target error, up to logarithmic factors. The result translates eventual convergence into a quantitative guarantee about the data needed for accurate robust evaluation.
neurips-2025-finite-sample-analysis-of-p.tldr: The paper gives order-optimal finite-sample guarantees for robust average-reward policy evaluation using controlled-bias, truncated Monte Carlo estimates.

paragraphs: GSO evaluates whether language-model software agents can make existing programs run faster. Each task supplies a codebase and a performance test, giving the agent a concrete optimization target. The resulting runtime improvement is measured against an optimization made by an expert developer, grounding the benchmark in demonstrated software improvements.

The authors build the tasks through an automated pipeline that generates and executes performance tests while examining repository commit histories. This process identifies 102 challenging tasks across 10 codebases, covering different domains and programming languages. The benchmark therefore tests performance engineering across varied software settings, with the performance test serving as a precise specification of the task.

Leading software agents achieve success rates below 5% in the reported evaluation, and additional inference-time computation brings only limited improvements. The qualitative analysis points to trouble with low-level languages, lazy optimization strategies, and locating actual bottlenecks. These findings identify concrete weaknesses in current agents' optimization abilities. Released benchmark artifacts and agent trajectories make those failures available for further study.
neurips-2025-gso-challenging-software-op.tldr: GSO tests software agents on 102 real optimization tasks, where leading agents succeed less than 5% of the time.

paragraphs: Curriculum learning organizes training examples so that a model encounters simpler material before harder material. This paper constructs that progression by starting with difficult examples and recursively generating easier versions. The reversal concerns how the curriculum is created: the student still learns through a progression intended to help it master increasingly difficult tasks.

A teacher model capable of step-by-step reasoning performs the decomposition. Its role is to turn complex dataset examples into simpler, more learnable components that can support student training. The authors also introduce a difficulty score based on structural complexity and conceptual depth. This score provides a basis for organizing the decomposed examples into a curriculum.

Experiments cover mathematical problems from MATH and AIME, along with code-generation datasets. Students trained with the generated curricula outperform models trained conventionally on the original datasets in these evaluations. The findings support using a reasoning-capable teacher to shape the learning sequence itself. They connect problem decomposition, difficulty assessment, and curriculum construction as parts of one training approach.
neurips-2025-learning-to-solve-complex-p.tldr: A reasoning-capable teacher builds learning curricula by recursively simplifying difficult examples, improving student performance on tested math and code tasks.

paragraphs: A classifier's probability estimates should reflect how often its predictions are correct. This paper studies that calibration problem for linear binary classifiers with Gaussian features. Its setting is high-dimensional: the number of examples and the number of features both grow, with neither becoming negligible relative to the other.

The proposed angular calibration interpolates the fitted classifier with a noninformative chance classifier. How much it interpolates depends on the angle between the estimated weight vector and the true weight vector. The authors show that this angle can be consistently estimated and prove calibration in the stated high-dimensional regime.

The predictor also satisfies an optimality property: within a suitable class of calibrated predictors, it uniquely minimizes a Bregman divergence from the true label distribution. This links reliable probabilities with a precise measure of distributional closeness. Finally, the paper identifies conditions under which classical Platt scaling converges to the same solution. Under those conditions, Platt scaling inherits the calibration and optimality guarantees, connecting the new theory to an established calibration approach.
neurips-2025-optimal-and-provable-calibr.tldr: Angular calibration provides provably calibrated and Bregman-optimal predictions in a Gaussian high-dimensional setting, with conditional guarantees for Platt scaling.

paragraphs: ORIGEN addresses control over the three-dimensional orientation of objects in generated images. Spatial control has often focused on where objects sit in the image plane; this work targets how they are oriented in space. The proposed zero-shot method supports multiple objects and diverse categories using pretrained components.

The system combines a discriminative model that estimates 3D orientation with a one-step text-to-image generative flow model. Orientation estimates provide a reward that guides generation. The authors find that directly maximizing this reward through gradient ascent struggles to preserve image realism. They instead use Langevin dynamics, which adds random noise to the gradient-based updates.

An additional adaptive time-rescaling mechanism uses the reward function to accelerate convergence. In the reported experiments, ORIGEN outperforms training-based approaches and test-time guidance methods on quantitative evaluations and user studies. The contribution is a sampling procedure that uses orientation feedback to guide image creation while addressing the realism difficulties encountered with direct reward maximization. It broadens spatial grounding to include object orientation as well as position.
neurips-2025-origen-zero-shot-3d-orienta.tldr: ORIGEN uses reward-guided noisy sampling to control multiple objects' 3D orientations in text-to-image generation without task-specific training.

paragraphs: Preference-based reinforcement learning learns from judgments about alternatives. This paper studies feedback that ranks several actions together, asking whether those richer rankings can improve sample efficiency. Previous theoretical guarantees did not consistently improve with longer feedback, leaving a gap between the information available and the benefits the theory could establish.

The authors assume a Plackett–Luce model for rankings and introduce M-AUPO. It chooses an action subset by maximizing the average uncertainty among its options. The resulting suboptimality bound decreases as the offered subsets become larger. For a fixed subset size, its stated dependence scales with the feature dimension divided by the square root of the number of rounds times the subset size, apart from logarithmic factors.

The bound also avoids exponential dependence on the unknown parameter's norm. A near-matching lower bound helps characterize the remaining difficulty of the problem. These are theoretical guarantees under the ranking model: they establish an explicit sample-efficiency benefit from larger subsets, giving a principled reason to study feedback beyond pairs.
neurips-2025-preference-based-reinforcem.tldr: Under a Plackett–Luce ranking model, M-AUPO provides guarantees that explicitly improve as feedback ranks larger action subsets.

paragraphs: ReAgent-V develops video understanding as an iterative process with feedback. A single reasoning pass offers little opportunity to revisit an initial answer, while existing reward and tool-based approaches face annotation, feedback, and efficiency challenges. The proposed framework combines efficient frame selection with rewards generated during inference to guide ongoing refinement.

Its reflection mechanism revisits predictions from conservative, neutral, and aggressive perspectives. The reward signals help direct those revisions and also filter high-quality data for subsequent training. The same framework supplies data for supervised fine-tuning, direct preference optimization, and group relative policy optimization, connecting inference-time feedback with later model improvement.

The design is modular and supports tools tailored to different tasks. Evaluations span 12 datasets and three applications: video understanding, video reasoning enhancement, and vision-language-action model alignment. The authors report improvements of up to 6.9%, 2.1%, and 9.8%, respectively, alongside gains in generalization and reasoning. These results support the usefulness of combining selective visual evidence, multiple reflection perspectives, and real-time rewards across the tested applications.
neurips-2025-reagent-v-a-reward-driven-m.tldr: ReAgent-V combines frame selection, real-time rewards, and multi-perspective reflection to refine video answers and select useful training data.

paragraphs: The paper examines whether Local Shapley Values and LIME reliably identify features that matter to a particular prediction. It argues that a feature should receive no importance if it neither affects the model's output nor depends statistically on features that do. The authors show that both methods can violate this principle even with exact computations and independent features.

Their alternative, R-LOCO, explains predictions through regions of the input space. It first groups inputs into regions with similar feature-importance characteristics. Global attribution methods then operate within each region, and an individual example receives feature contributions according to its regional membership. This makes the region the working unit for attribution.

The approach connects detailed explanations of individual predictions with importance estimates over groups of examples. According to the paper, it provides more faithful local attributions while avoiding instability in local explanations and retaining detail that global summaries can lose. The contribution includes both a critique of established attribution methods and a regional construction intended to address the identified failure.
neurips-2025-regional-explanations-bridg.tldr: R-LOCO explains predictions using regional feature importance to address faithfulness failures identified in Local Shapley Values and LIME.

paragraphs: Peer prediction encourages honest feedback by comparing participants' reports with those of their peers when ground truth cannot be checked. Traditional guarantees make honesty maximize expected scores in equilibrium. Those guarantees fit linear utility, but nonlinear payment rules or personal preferences can change how participants value the same score distribution.

The paper proposes stochastically dominant truthfulness, requiring the distribution of honest-reporting scores to dominate those from alternative strategies. This supports honesty for a broad range of monotone utility functions. Converting scores into binary lotteries can enforce the property, but often weakens sensitivity, which matters for fairness and statistical efficiency. The authors show how more careful rounding better preserves that sensitivity.

They also introduce an enforced agreement mechanism with a theoretical guarantee of this stronger truthfulness in binary-signal settings. Under mild assumptions, it empirically achieves the highest sensitivity among known mechanisms satisfying the criterion. The work separates the strength of an honesty guarantee from the sensitivity of the scoring system, then develops mechanisms intended to achieve both.
neurips-2025-stochastically-dominant-pee.tldr: The paper develops stronger peer-prediction incentives that support honest reporting under nonlinear utilities while better preserving score sensitivity.

paragraphs: Vision-language models can recognize categories without task-specific training, yet their performance can fall when test images differ from familiar domains. Spectrum-Aware Test-Time Steering, or STS, adapts a model to one unlabeled image at a time. It performs this adaptation in latent representations while keeping the image and text encoders frozen.

STS extracts a spectral subspace from text embeddings to identify principal semantic directions. It then learns a small set of shifts for the current sample, steering representations according to that structure. The shifts are optimized to reduce prediction entropy across augmented views of the image, without backpropagating through the encoders or changing their weights.

Across the reported evaluations, STS generally surpasses or compares favorably with leading test-time adaptation methods. Against conventional test-time prompt tuning, it achieves inference speeds up to eight times faster and a twelvefold smaller memory footprint. These findings support using semantic structure in the latent space to obtain useful adaptation with only a handful of additional parameters and substantially reduced computational demands.
neurips-2025-test-time-spectrum-aware-la.tldr: STS adapts frozen vision-language models through small latent shifts, reporting competitive accuracy with much lower inference time and memory use.

paragraphs: This paper develops iterative polynomial filtering, an outlier-removal algorithm for supervised learning with contaminated training data. Its first result applies when a function class has low-degree polynomial approximations under a hypercontractive distribution. Under those conditions, the class can be learned efficiently with bounded contamination, extending the usefulness of such approximations beyond tolerance to corrupted labels.

A second result handles heavy additive contamination, where adversarially added examples can constitute far more than half the training set. This stronger result requires sandwiching approximators, a stronger approximation condition, and delivers near-optimal learning guarantees. The distinction matters: the paper connects different levels of contamination tolerance to different mathematical properties of the function class.

The authors also establish efficient tolerant testable learning algorithms for functions of halfspaces under any fixed log-concave distribution. Even the non-tolerant single-halfspace case had remained open in that setting. Together, these results show that one filtering approach can support several supervised-learning guarantees, with each guarantee tied to its stated approximation or distributional assumptions.
neurips-2025-the-power-of-iterative-filt.tldr: Iterative polynomial filtering enables efficient supervised learning under several contamination models, including heavy contamination under stronger approximation assumptions.

paragraphs: Thinkless trains a language model to decide whether a query needs a short response or extended reasoning. The motivation is computational: applying a long reasoning process to every problem can waste effort on straightforward questions. Its choice depends on both the difficulty of the task and the model's own ability to solve it.

Two control tokens signal the available reasoning modes. Training uses Decoupled Group Relative Policy Optimization, which separates the objective for choosing a mode from the objective for producing accurate answers. This separation lets the contributions of the two objectives be controlled independently. The authors report that it stabilizes learning and prevents the collapse observed with vanilla GRPO.

On benchmarks including Minerva Algebra, MATH-500, and GSM8K, Thinkless reduces the use of long-chain thinking by 50% to 90%. That reported reduction concerns how often the model invokes extended reasoning. The approach makes reasoning length a learned decision within the model and demonstrates that selective use of long reasoning can substantially improve efficiency on the evaluated tasks.
neurips-2025-thinkless-llm-learns-when-t.tldr: Thinkless learns to choose short or extended reasoning, reducing long-chain thinking by 50%–90% on the reported benchmarks.

paragraphs: SCR investigates whether training on knowledge graphs can produce a model useful across many other graph tasks. Existing graph foundation models often need additional fine-tuning to apply what they have learned to new graphs. The paper takes inspiration from zero-shot inductive knowledge-graph reasoning and develops a unified framework for broader transfer.

The framework first constructs task-specific knowledge-graph structures that give different task formats a shared topology. It then uses semantic-conditioned message passing to combine structural and semantic patterns in graph representations. This mechanism addresses semantic isolation in traditional knowledge-graph reasoning, allowing meaning and connectivity to contribute jointly to transferable representations.

The evaluation covers 38 datasets with tasks involving individual nodes, links, and entire graphs. SCR achieves substantial gains over the existing foundation models and supervised baselines considered in those experiments. The findings support knowledge-graph training as a route toward reusable graph reasoning. They also connect that transfer to two design choices: expressing tasks through compatible structures and incorporating semantics directly into message passing.
neurips-2025-towards-graph-foundation-mo.tldr: SCR combines unified task structures with semantic-conditioned message passing to transfer knowledge-graph training across diverse graph tasks.

paragraphs: This paper studies learning in multiplayer games when each player receives bandit feedback and follows strongly uncoupled dynamics. The aim is to support modular learning while obtaining both no-regret behavior and convergence of the latest decisions. Last-iterate convergence matters because it concerns the players' current actions, rather than only an average over their learning history.

For smooth monotone games, the authors propose a mirror-descent-based algorithm with a convergence rate of order T to the minus one-quarter, where T is the number of rounds. The algorithm also satisfies a no-regret guarantee. Its analysis relies on two regularizations and their associated fixed point. Under the stronger assumption of strong monotonicity, the convergence rate improves to order T to the minus one-half.

The framework extends to games that change over time. The paper provides a non-asymptotic result for converging monotone games and improved equilibrium-tracking results. These guarantees distinguish stable learning in a fixed game from following changing equilibria, while retaining the limited-feedback and decentralized learning setting.
neurips-2025-uncoupled-and-convergent-le.tldr: A mirror-descent algorithm achieves no regret and last-iterate convergence in monotone games with bandit feedback and strongly uncoupled learning.

paragraphs: Large pretrained vision models contain useful representations, but applying them to specialized scientific tasks with little data remains challenging. CLAdapter aims to adapt those representations to the particular feature sets encountered downstream. The contribution is an adapter that refines pretrained features during fine-tuning across varied scientific settings.

Its mechanism combines attention with cluster centers. Distribution correlations and transformation matrices guide how transformed features are enhanced, allowing different feature sets to receive distinct adaptations. This makes the transfer process responsive to the representations being adapted. A unified interface supports integration with both convolutional networks and Transformers in two-dimensional and three-dimensional contexts.

The authors evaluate CLAdapter on 10 datasets covering a broad range of scientific and other visual settings, including biological, medical, industrial, and geographical applications, as well as out-of-distribution and 3D analysis. They report state-of-the-art performance across the evaluated data-limited domains. The results support adapting rich pretrained features through a shared adapter design that can accommodate different architectures and downstream feature distributions.
neurips-2025-unleashing-foundation-visio.tldr: CLAdapter uses cluster-guided attention to adapt pretrained vision features across diverse scientific tasks with limited training data.

paragraphs: Multimodal alignment often depends on millions of paired examples, which can be difficult to obtain in specialized domains. This paper instead aligns existing unimodal foundation models using much smaller paired datasets. It shows high-quality alignment with tens of thousands of pairs, less than 1% of the amount typically used in the field.

The proposed STRUCTURE regularizer preserves neighborhood geometry in the encoders' latent spaces during alignment. This carries information about relationships among representations into the alignment process. A second component selects layers with the greatest representational similarity across modalities. The authors find that aligning final layers is often suboptimal, making layer selection another useful part of the method.

Both components can be incorporated into existing alignment approaches. Across 24 zero-shot image-classification and retrieval benchmarks, the paper reports average relative improvements of 51.6% for classification and 91.8% for retrieval. These results support combining structural preservation with compatible layer selection when paired data is scarce. The gains are reported as relative improvements, describing changes against the evaluated alignment methods.
neurips-2025-with-limited-data-for-multi.tldr: Preserving latent neighborhood structure and aligning compatible layers enables strong multimodal alignment with tens of thousands of paired examples.

paragraphs: Static tokenizers can split domain-specific or language-specific text into unnecessarily long sequences. zip2zip lets a language model adapt its active vocabulary to the current context during inference. It replaces recurring fragmented sequences with compact hypertokens that the model can use in both its inputs and generated outputs.

The method uses Lempel–Ziv–Welch compression to merge co-occurring tokens incrementally. A dynamic embedding and unembedding layer constructs representations for new hypertokens at runtime. A modified autoregressive training objective prepares the model to process and produce these compressed sequences. These components connect vocabulary growth with the model's ability to use newly created units immediately.

The authors show that an existing language model can be adapted for zip2zip through parameter-efficient fine-tuning in 10 GPU-hours. Once prepared, the model learns to use hypertokens in unseen contexts at test time, reducing input and output token counts by 15% to 40%. The finding demonstrates context-sensitive compression within language-model operation, with adaptation happening during inference after the required model preparation.
neurips-2025-zip2zip-inference-time-adap.tldr: zip2zip learns to create and use compressed hypertokens at inference time, reducing input and output token counts by 15%–40%.
